name: Morocco
summary: Muslim estates follow the Family Code (Moudawana) fixed shares, with only up to one third freely bequeathed. A non-Muslim foreigner's inheritance is governed by their national law (art. 332). Trusts and foundations were not sourced.
reserved_share: Muslims: Islamic fixed shares (fara'id) apply to two thirds; a bequest to a non-heir is limited to one third (practitioner guide). No inheritance between Muslim and non-Muslim.
foreign_law_note: Reported: art. 332 of the Family Code subjects foreigners' inheritance to their national personal law; non-Muslim foreigners keep their national law unless they opt for Moroccan law; Muslim foreigners' Moroccan assets follow Islamic law whatever their nationality. Moroccan Jews follow the Moroccan Hebrew code.
trust_note: Moroccan civil-law fiducie is believed to exist since 2007 but was not sourced; no general trust law; foundations not found (habous/waqf exists).
open_questions: Whether the fiducie exists and its scope not sourced.
Article 332 as paraphrased by secondary sources; verify the text.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.
